facts.value: GRE General Test is not considered for all 14 Home Programs. GRE Subject Test is optional only for Biophysics (Mathematics or Physics); it is not considered for the other 13.

facts.value: Most Home Programs have no specific coursework admission requirement. Biomedical Data Science, Biophysics, Molecular and Cellular Physiology, and Structural Biology have course background requirements; applicants should contact each program for specifics.

conditions: Prior life-sciences undergraduate preparation is common but not required; applicants may come from chemistry, computer science, mathematics, psychology, physics, or other fields.

facts.value: The shared application requests academic record, admissions essays, recommendation letters, prior research experience entered in the Experience section, and current Resume/CV. Up to six significant experiences may be listed; coursework laboratory sections are excluded. Unrequested supplemental publications or theses are not used.

scope.policy_family: Fourteen named Biosciences PhD Home Programs, explicitly including H&S Biology and Biophysics

conditions: All letters and application materials should arrive by deadline; late materials may not be reviewed.

facts.value: Selected applicants are invited for the only interview session, March 3-6, 2027; Stanford pays interview costs. Invitations begin mid-January and continue through mid-February. Highly qualified international applicants unable to travel may be selected for a virtual interview.

scope.policy_family: Fourteen named Biosciences PhD Home Programs, explicitly including H&S Biology and Biophysics

facts.value: Offer letters are sent mid-March 2027; offer acceptance deadline is April 15, 2027. Applicants not invited to interview by mid-February are unlikely to be invited or admitted; non-invitees receive a no-further-action letter.

facts.value: The 2026-27 admission offer included stipend $58,460 ($14,615/quarter), health and dental insurance, and graduate tuition, conditional on Stanford enrollment and good academic standing. 2027-28 stipend and benefits not yet set; page says they will be set in March 2027.

scope.policy_family: Fourteen named Biosciences PhD Home Programs, explicitly including H&S Biology and Biophysics

conditions: Do not project the 2026-27 amount into the 2027-28 cycle.

facts.value: For the 2027-28 cohort, Round 1 opens September 15, 2026 and closes November 9, 2026; Round 2 runs November 10, 2026 through January 11, 2027. Decisions are expected in January and March 2027. Round 1 applicants with incomplete materials roll to Round 2; the Round 2 materials deadline is firm. Knight-Hennessy consideration requires a separate application by its own deadline.
conditions: MCiM Round 1 is required for concurrent Knight-Hennessy consideration; KHS application and deadline are separate.
exceptions: Incomplete Round 1 applications roll to Round 2; incomplete Round 2 applications remain incomplete.

facts.value: The 2027-28 cohort begins on campus in June 2027 and runs Summer 2026-27 through Spring 2027-28 for 12 months. Applicants select Summer 2026-27 in the Stanford portal; the cohort does not permit an off-cycle start.
exceptions: Portal entry term label is Summer 2026-27 although cohort is named 2027-28 and starts June 2027.

facts.value: GRE is not required; applicants may submit scores. English test scores are required unless one of Stanford's four waiver categories applies. The application requires unofficial postsecondary transcripts, three recommendations, a CV, statement of purpose (max 2 pages), learning-community statement (max 500 words), time-management essay, and a personal financial plan. Selected candidates complete a one-way video interview and a Zoom committee interview.
conditions: If applicant is at most five years out of school at cohort start, one recommender must be faculty from the last full-time school; after five years, faculty recommendation is not required.
exceptions: Official transcripts are required after offer; applicant-uploaded official transcripts are not accepted.

facts.value: The published 2026-27 rate estimate totals $86,625 for four quarters: Summer at $21,180 (2025-26 rate) and the remaining quarters at $21,815 each (2026-27 rate). Miscellaneous fees and living costs are additional. MCiM reports no departmental scholarship awards; students may explore financial aid, loans, external scholarships, family, or government resources.
conditions: Summer uses the prior academic year's tuition rate; remaining quarters use 2026-27 rates.
exceptions: This tuition estimate excludes living expenses and additional university fees.
2027-28 tuition rates were not confirmed in the reviewed source.

facts.value: CHPR requires at least 45 units and most students complete it in one academic year, Autumn through Summer. The program includes community-based research internship and a master's thesis. The Prevention Research Center states it currently has no funding available for MS students.

applicant_categories: current Stanford graduate or professional students

conditions: Current Stanford graduate and professional students may apply on a rolling basis; up to 45 CHPR units may count toward Stanford PhD requirements.
exceptions: Funding statement has no explicit cycle; verify before presenting as current for a later intake.

facts.value: For Autumn 2027 coterm entry, application and all materials are due January 19, 2027. Applicants normally apply in junior or senior year after completing 120 units; only under unusual circumstances may the committee review a late petition. Required items are CV, statement of purpose, three letters, and unofficial Stanford transcript. GRE is recommended but not required, though it may be requested when quantitative coursework is limited; TOEFL is not required. Decisions are expected by mid-April and coterm deferrals are not allowed.
conditions: Two references should be from current department or Epidemiology & Population Health faculty and one from academic advisor.
exceptions: Late review is petition-only and limited to unusual circumstances; complete materials remain required.
Courses from Autumn of sophomore year onward may be considered for transfer to the MS; earlier courses cannot satisfy MS requirements.

facts.value: Human Genetics and Genetic Counseling has no required prerequisite courses, though preparation in psychology, biochemistry, molecular biology, genetics, and statistics is encouraged. GRE is entirely optional and applicants who omit it are not disadvantaged. Only three completed reference surveys are reviewed.
exceptions: Recommended preparation is not a formal course prerequisite.

facts.value: For Fall 2026 starters the FAQ lists total tuition of $109,269. It describes work-study positions providing about $15,000 tuition remission across the program, typically six additional $5,000-$10,000 scholarships selected by program ranking without a separate application, plus education stipend and research-project funds. The page estimates tuition may rise about 3% for 2027, but the estimate is not guaranteed.
conditions: Scholarships are selected by program ranking and available funds; no separate application is required.
exceptions: 2027 tuition increase is an estimate; actual rates and funding vary by cycle.

facts.value: For 2027-28, applications are due January 29, 2027. M-TRAM does not require GRE. English proficiency evidence is required before enrollment unless waived under Stanford policy. Selected applicants are interviewed by program directors.
conditions: Knight-Hennessy scholarship consideration requires a separate KHS application by October 6, 2026, earlier than the M-TRAM deadline.
exceptions: The reviewed page also displays a historical Jan 30, 2026 deadline and $125 2026-27 application fee; the current 2027-28 fee was not confirmed.

facts.value: Stanford Bulletin code BMDS-MS covers distinct Academic (research) MS, Honors Cooperative Program professional MS, and coterm MS routes. The Academic MS is full-time, normally two years, with at least 50% research effort and a written research paper approved by two faculty. The coterm MS is only for current Stanford undergraduates. The HCP professional MS is excluded from this dossier and handled in the professional-program dossier. GRE is not required.

For the 2027-28 MS Health Policy application cycle, GRE or, for physicians, MCAT is required. Applicants seeking Knight-Hennessy funding must also submit a separate KHS application by its earlier deadline.
conditions: MS and PhD Health Policy have separate applications and train different skills; apply to the target degree, not both by assumption.

facts.value: Health Policy PhD and MS use separate applications. PhD has no minimum GPA; all application materials and letters must be received by the published deadline. Offer includes stipend, health insurance, and graduate tuition; annual amounts are set in early March before the academic year.
conditions: Health Policy PhD route and deadline must be checked on its own directory entry; the shared Biosciences application does not apply to this PhD.

facts.value: Laboratory Animal Science accepts one application per year for Fall only. Fall 2027 application opened September 15, 2026 and closes December 4, 2026. External applicants apply through Graduate Admissions and select thesis or non-thesis track. GRE is not required. Application fee is $125, non-refundable, due by deadline. Three recommendation letters and statement of purpose (maximum two single-spaced pages) are required; an optional learning-community statement may be up to 500 words.

Coterm applicants use the program process in the same published cycle and select thesis or non-thesis track; expected GPA is at least 3.0. The department says complete coterm decisions usually arrive 2-3 weeks after the deadline. Current Stanford graduate, doctoral, and medical students use a separate internal online application; petitions are due by the last day of the quarter requested and incur a service fee regardless of outcome. Stanford PhD students may count up to 45 MLAS units toward PhD residency, except when they already received graduate residency transfer credit for a prior master degree.

applicant_categories: current Stanford graduate, doctoral, and medical students

conditions: Coterm decision must be accepted in the same quarter; contact the department for exact acceptance deadline.
exceptions: Current postdoctoral scholars are not eligible for the internal route and must apply externally.

facts.value: The Academic Biomedical Data Science MS may have NLM-funded positions for postdoctoral trainees; other applicants may apply, but department funding is not guaranteed. This is distinct from the PhD offer funding and from the HCP professional MS tuition model.

scope.cycle: current program description; cycle not specified

conditions: NLM-funded positions are identified for postdoctoral trainees.
exceptions: Funding for other applicants is not guaranteed.

facts.value: SCBRM page says its applicants select two Biosciences programs as first and second choice and that SCBRM preferentially considers applicants naming it first. The current shared Biosciences application page also permits a primary and one alternative Home Program. SCBRM identifies KHS as a separate application with October 6, 2026 deadline; eligible candidates must have earned their first undergraduate degree within the last seven years. KHS can provide full funding for up to three years of PhD study.
conditions: KHS is separate from Stanford PhD admission and has its own earlier deadline.
exceptions: The SCBRM page says two program choices while the shared Biosciences page says up to three; verify the 2027-28 portal choice count with Biosciences Admissions before applying.

facts.value: SCBRM MS is not a terminal external MS application. Existing program PhD students may apply for the MS after satisfactorily completing first-two-year coursework, laboratory requirements, and the qualifying exam. A 2024-25 program handbook also describes an MS as a terminal degree for students unable to meet PhD milestones after remediation.
conditions: Bulletin says the award is only open to existing STMRM-PHD students.
exceptions: Remediation/terminal-award path is documented in a 2024-25 handbook and needs confirmation against the current handbook.

facts.value: Official Graduate Application Program List gives an Autumn 2027-28 application deadline of Dec 1, 2026. Testing row: GRE general and subject are not considered for the academic MS.
Official Graduate Application Program List gives an Autumn 2027-28 application deadline of Jan 7, 2027. Testing row: GRE general test is optional; GRE subject test is not considered.
Official Graduate Application Program List gives an Autumn 2027-28 application deadline of Feb 2, 2027. Testing row: GRE general test is optional; GRE subject test is not considered.

Official Graduate Application Program List gives an Autumn 2027-28 application deadline of Jan 21, 2027. Testing row: GRE general test is required for the 2027-28 MS cycle; GRE subject test is not considered.
Official Graduate Application Program List gives an Autumn 2027-28 application deadline of Dec 1, 2026. Testing row: GRE general test is optional; GRE subject test is not considered.

For external Autumn 2027-28 applicants: U.S. or equivalent international bachelor degree; three recommendation letters (one recent-school faculty unless out of school >5 years); GRE or MCAT optional; CV; 1-2 page statement; unofficial transcripts from every postsecondary school attended full-time for at least one year; $125 application fee. All materials must arrive by deadline or application is not reviewed. CHPR English minimum is higher than Stanford general minimum: TOEFL 110 before Jan 21, 2026 / 5.5 on/after Jan 21, 2026, or IELTS 8.
exceptions: TOEFL/IELTS waiver categories and timing follow Stanford graduate policy; CHPR page says applicants whose first language is not English may need a score.

facts.value: Coterm is only for current Stanford undergraduates with at least 120 units toward graduation, a declared major, and six non-summer Stanford quarters (two for transfer students). At least one quarter of overlap is required. Materials: online coterm application, 1-2 page statement, two Stanford professor letters, CV, preliminary program proposal, Stanford transcript. GRE is not required. A $125 fee is charged by the Registrar only if admitted and accepting.
conditions: All coterm admits matriculate Autumn only.
exceptions: Program page allows transfer of eligible CHPR courses and one approved methods elective from three non-summer quarters back; both CHPR and undergraduate major must approve transfers.

facts.value: Current Stanford graduate and professional degree students (including medical students) may apply on a rolling basis; priority is the first Tuesday in May for Autumn matriculation. Postdocs must use the external route. Materials: program form, CV, unofficial transcript, 1-2 page statement, two Stanford faculty letters; applicant may be interviewed. $125 fee applies only if admitted and accepting. PhD students may count up to 45 CHPR units toward residency unless they have used graduate residency transfer credit for another master degree.

applicant_categories: current Stanford graduate and professional students

exceptions: Current Stanford postdoctoral scholars are excluded from this internal route and apply externally.

facts.value: The Epidemiology department has limited funding available for MS and PhD students; awards are made at admission by the program coordinator. Applicants are encouraged to seek external or Stanford fellowships; research or teaching assistantships may be discussed with faculty after acceptance. Coterm students retain undergraduate aid access through the 12th quarter/four years; after 180 units they may be eligible for University fellowships and assistantships, but awards are not guaranteed and many require the bachelor degree.

Health Policy MS students typically complete the degree in 5-6 quarters; 8-10 units per quarter is full-time. Tuition is set annually by Stanford and applicants are directed to current Registrar graduate tuition rates; the program page does not state a program-specific fixed total.
exceptions: Exact tuition for the applicable cycle requires the current Registrar rate table and student unit plan.

facts.value: M-TRAM is a four-quarter program: three full-time quarters at 11-18 units and one summer quarter at 10 units. The reviewed official page lists a $79,625 estimated tuition total based on 2025-26 rates ($65,445 for three full-time quarters plus $14,180 summer). M-TRAM reports no departmental scholarship awards; students may explore Stanford financial aid, loans, outside scholarships, family or government support.
conditions: Annual tuition updates occur in Autumn.
exceptions: 2026-27 and 2027-28 actual total tuition is not given on the reviewed cost page; do not present the $79,625 as the current cycle cost.

facts.value: The Autumn 2027-28 Biosciences application asks for one primary degree program and permits one alternative Home Program. Applicants rank 8-12 faculty, mostly in the primary Home Program; no supervisor is required before applying.

scope.policy_family: Fourteen named Biosciences PhD Home Programs, explicitly including H&S Biology and Biophysics

facts.value: All DBDS graduate degrees expect one year of calculus, one probability/statistics course, linear algebra, one year of computer science centered on fundamentals, and some biology or medicine coursework. Multivariable calculus and separate probability and statistics courses are preferred.
Academic BMDS MS is full-time and on campus, requires 45 Stanford units plus a research project, and normally lasts 1.5-2 years. Research rotations are encouraged during the first year.

NLM support for the Academic MS is limited to postdoctoral scholars who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents; others must secure outside support or self-fund. Non-postdoctoral applicants have no guaranteed DBDS funding.

HCP BMDS MS is part-time distance education with no DBDS financial aid. Applications use the Biosciences form and may start in Autumn, Winter, or Spring: deadlines are October 16, 2026 for Winter, January 15, 2027 for Spring, and April 30, 2027 for Autumn. GRE general and subject scores are not considered.
conditions: No Summer start.

facts.value: Current Stanford undergraduates apply through the coterminal portal while undergraduate status remains active. Autumn, Winter, and Spring entry deadlines are April 30, 2027; October 16, 2026; and January 15, 2027 respectively. Stanford transcript, 1-2 page statement, CV, two recommendations, proposed course plan and prerequisite evidence are requested. GRE and TOEFL are not required.
conditions: No Summer application.
Research project and rotations are optional for coterm MS.

facts.value: Currently enrolled Stanford graduate students, including medical students, may add the BMDS MS by sending DBDS a Graduate Authorization Petition, two recommendations, transcripts, CV, 1-2 page statement, supplemental form, and course flowsheet. Rolling review uses first day of August, November, February, or May as the quarter-specific submission deadline.

BMDS PhD is full-time residential research study, averaging about five years; no part-time or distance PhD is offered. Students in good standing receive a stipend, tuition and health insurance for the duration through mixed fellowship, dean and research-assistant funding, and are expected to seek internal and external awards.

For Autumn 2027 entry the BMP PhD deadline is November 30, 2026. Applicants need a bachelor's degree in engineering or physical science (or international equivalent), mathematics through multivariable calculus and linear algebra, unofficial transcripts, a 1-2 page personal statement, CV and recommendations. GRE general and subject scores are not required or considered; English proficiency follows Stanford policy where applicable.

BMP is a full-time residential research PhD with first-year lab rotations, qualifying examination by the end of year two, and dissertation; the program describes a typical 5-6 years. Students making satisfactory academic progress receive tuition and living stipend throughout the doctorate. External fellowships are encouraged but not required.

Epidemiology and Clinical Research PhD applications and all recommendations are due December 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. through Stanford Graduate Admissions. Required materials are statement of purpose, three recommendations, unofficial transcripts, CV, and English test if not exempt. GRE is optional but encouraged; official transcripts are required only after an offer is accepted.

The Epidemiology department has limited MS and PhD funding, awarded at admission; prospective PhD students are encouraged to seek external and Stanford funding. Research or teaching assistantships may be discussed with individual professors after acceptance. Training grants support selected research areas, but PhD students need not join one.

The Epidemiology and Clinical Research MS is full-time and on campus, typically five to six quarters over two years. It requires 45 graduate units, a thesis normally based on original epidemiology research, overall B average, and B- or better in each core course.

Health Policy PhD students are guaranteed funding for the first five years; support can combine fellowships, grants, research assistantships and teaching assistantships. Admission capacity depends on available funding.

For Fall 2027 entry, the Human Genetics and Genetic Counseling MS deadline is December 1, 2026. Applicants must register with the Genetic Counseling Admissions Match before applying. The Stanford application requests a $125 fee, three short recommender surveys rather than letters, CV, personal statement, supplemental essay, transcripts and English scores if applicable. Match results are binding and released in late April.
Beginning in 2027 the Laboratory Animal Science MS offers thesis and non-thesis tracks. Stanford undergraduates may pursue it as a coterminal degree.

applicant_categories: external and current Stanford undergraduate applicants

facts.value: The Autumn 2027-28 Biosciences PhD application fee is $125 and non-refundable. Eligible applicants may request a Graduate Admissions waiver; international applicants may seek the School-Based waiver.

scope.policy_family: Fourteen named Biosciences PhD Home Programs, explicitly including H&S Biology and Biophysics

facts.value: Biosciences PhD students complete at least two laboratory rotations; the recommended number and length vary by Home Program. Most coursework is completed in the first year, followed by research specialization and dissertation work.

scope.policy_family: Fourteen named Biosciences PhD Home Programs, explicitly including H&S Biology and Biophysics

facts.value: MCP asks for a bachelor's or master's degree in any major, coursework in physiology, cell/developmental biology, basic biochemistry and molecular biology, and genetics, plus at least one university year each in physics, differential/integral calculus, and organic/inorganic chemistry. Research experience in biological sciences is especially valued.

Structural Biology PhD applicants need a bachelor's degree with at least one year of coursework in each of biology, mathematics, organic chemistry, physical chemistry, and physics. Original undergraduate research is particularly valued; GRE general and subject scores are not considered.

The 2026-27 Bulletin requires at least 46 program units and 135 university PhD units. Core epidemiology and biostatistics coursework precedes a written examination near the end of year two and an oral qualifying examination by Autumn of year three, then dissertation research. The Bulletin reports typical completion in four to four-and-a-half years.

For Autumn 2027-28 Health Policy PhD entry, the official application directory lists December 1, 2026 as the deadline and GRE General Test as required; no GRE Subject Test is considered. The program FAQ specifies no minimum GRE score and accepts scores up to three weeks after the deadline only when the test was taken before the deadline.

Health Policy PhD requires a U.S. bachelor's degree or international equivalent, online Stanford application with recommendations by the deadline, and a statement of purpose of at most two single-spaced pages identifying track and policy interests. No master's or minimum GPA is required. The program is full-time and in person; applying to the separate MS does not automatically follow from a PhD application.

Health Policy MS applicants should have clinical, healthcare, government or similar professional experience, though a medical degree is not required. The program is full-time and in person and offers no departmental fellowships or scholarships. U.S.-licensed physicians may substitute MCAT for GRE; exceptional GRE waivers require direct program approval.

The official coterm directory lists January 7, 2027 as the deadline for Autumn 2027-28 Community Health and Prevention Research MS entry, with two recommendations and a required program proposal. The program page limits coterm matriculation to Autumn and expects all materials by the deadline.

MCiM has no minimum GPA. Three recommendations are required; applicants who left full-time school within five years of June 2027 must include one recommendation from faculty at their last full-time school. Candidates whose last full-time study ended earlier need no faculty recommender.

The Human Genetics and Genetic Counseling MS is a two-year translational program combining coursework, research projects and clinical fieldwork rotations. It admits Fall entrants only; no formal part-time or fully remote route is offered.

Laboratory Animal Science MS is designed as a two-year program. From 2027, applicants choose thesis or non-thesis track; both require 45 units, at least 36 at 200 level or above. Thesis students complete mentored research and a final thesis, while non-thesis students complete quarter-long projects.

applicant_categories: external and current Stanford undergraduate applicants

facts.value: For Autumn 2027-28 EPI MS entry, application and recommendations are due February 2, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific. The portal requests statement of purpose, three recommendations, CV, transcripts, optional GRE or other test scores, and TOEFL/IELTS if not exempt. Current Stanford MDs and MD students can request prior approval for exceptional late consideration; KHS applicants must submit the degree application by December 1, 2026 despite the regular February deadline.
conditions: KHS has its own earlier October 6, 2026 application deadline.

facts.value: EPI MS says applicants with non-U.S. academic credentials need a WES equivalency evaluation, while Stanford requires unofficial transcripts for review and original official transcripts after acceptance. Current Stanford students need not resend Stanford official transcripts but should provide prior institutional records.

applicant_categories: external graduate applicants with non-U.S. credentials

facts.value: M-TRAM asks for an accredited bachelor's degree, GPA at least 3.0 (3.5 recommended), CV covering clinical/basic research or biotechnology/pharma experience, three references, a statement of purpose up to 1,000 words, supplemental questions and transcripts. GRE is not required; selected candidates interview with program directors. The 2027-28 cohort begins September 20, 2027.
M-TRAM states a $125 non-refundable Stanford Graduate Admissions application fee; M-TRAM does not offer a program fee waiver, while university waivers may be available by separate eligibility.
Molecular and Cellular Physiology states that its PhD takes five to six years on average. There is no minimum GPA and GRE scores are not considered.

Human Genetics and Genetic Counseling sets no specific prerequisite courses, but recommends current genetics and counseling knowledge, relevant biology, biochemistry, psychology and statistics preparation, and exposure to the genetic counseling profession. Shadowing is valued but alternatives such as meetings, seminars and workshops are recognized.
